content:
- Model tends to overestimate prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially after recent spikes.
- Forecast often peaks too early and then declines too sharply, missing the true mean-reversion path.
- Model underestimates prices during sharp downward corrections following high peaks.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly in the 70–75 range, suggesting calibration drift.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows significant lag in capturing true price momentum; model reacts too slowly to recent volatility.
- Overshoot after spikes is common — model forecasts peak higher than true outcome, then drops below, indicating poor volatility decay modeling.
- Mean reversion is not adequately captured; model holds high values longer than observed in true data.
- Model fails to adjust downward when recent history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., after 73+ values).
- Forecast tends to ignore recent low values in history, leading to overconfidence in upward continuation.
- Model is sensitive to recent high values but underweights low values, causing persistent overestimation in mid-range forecasts.
